summary: A 1898 light on a granite pier in the lower Kennebec River, moved out to the point in 1899; automated 1988 and cared for by Friends since 1998.

structures.note: Moved 532 ft to a granite pier in September 1899 (Lighthouse Board; LighthouseFriends); reoriented 1899 (NRHP)
L-shaped; moved nearer the tower in 1901 (Lighthouse Board; NRHP)

access.note: Not open to the public (USLHS). The dwelling is privately owned (LighthouseFriends). Public cruises pass the light. A walkway collapsed in September 2023, injuring eleven visitors.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends gives Merritt Pinkham's start as 1889 in one place and 1898 in another. The station opened in 1898 and the USLHS roster gives 1898, so the story uses 1898.

The Lighthouse Service bulletins of 1912 and 1928 name keepers of 'Doubling Point Range light station'. Those are the range lights on Fiddlers Reach, a separate station (USLHS lists it as a separate place with its own roster), not this light.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-22. Fixed in the story: (1) scan page 294 (title acquired; station to be completed by February 1898) lies inside the Board report for the year ended June 30, 1897, whose header is at scan page 245, so the story now says 1897, not 1896 (the earlier note that the year came from the corpus label is resolved); (2) meta phrasing about sources removed; (3) footnotes added to sentences that carried none (the busy river, the 1895 appropriation, the 1899 move, the two keepers, the 1898 roster, the 1933 decision, the 1980 fog bell). Verified: the NRHP nomination itself gives 'Date Listed: 1/21/88' and the west side of Arrowsic Island, so the listing date stays footnoted to [1]. Board passages checked against scan pages: 1892 (pages 377-378, inside the FY1892 report that starts at scan page 328); 1895 (page 226); 1900 (pages 23 and 50; the move is dated 25 September 1899); 1901 (page 72); 1899 (page 80, the range lights at the lower end of Fiddlers Reach). Bulletins: 1912 PDF page 40 (Pierce, assistance) and 1928 PDF page 7 (Nye, rescue). Open items: (a) the 2023 walkway collapse and the five hospital cases come from LighthouseFriends only; not checked in a newspaper; (b) the 1935 buyer is not named; (c) Pinkham's start year is 1889 in one LighthouseFriends passage and 1898 in another, and the roster gives 1898; the story uses 1898; (d) Pinkham's and Allen's earlier service at Seguin and Eagle Island is not dated, so it is not in other_stations; (e) the Doubling Point Range station is a separate station with its own record and roster; the 1912 and 1928 bulletin keepers (Pierce, Nye) are not on this light's roster; (f) current optic: USLHS lists a solar LED optic installed 2017, not in the story; (g) Wikipedia read for leads only and not cited; (h) Chronicling America searches returned hits that did not match the snippets, none read beyond the snippets; (i) the 1898 opening has no Board passage beyond the 1896-1900 entries in the corpus.
